dataset: huggan/CelebA-faces-with-attributes @ b47e27a7 (real CelebA-aligned images; 11 of 132 upstream parquet shards are corrupt and were skipped, recorded in the manifest)

run1_10_mixed_signatures.verdict: weak/ambiguous cues (Reddish_Hair = 'no named hair color + wavy', Smiling_Young, ...); g failed to fit even training faces

run3_8_strong_cues_INVALID.verdict: all results invalid: a save_unlearning_adapter bug silently kept run1 checkpoints; the run3 evaluations scored run1 weights against the new manifest (g gate 0.062 was an artifact). Bug fixed in ef52466; outputs removed.

association_level_results.scope: codes derived from real CelebA images; h (C->Y) evaluated by exact code prompts, independent of g routing

gated_distance_to_leave_one_out_oracle.changed_ids: L2 1.24-1.41, reliable=true (far from oracle, which retains them; refusal/generalization edits are NOT oracle-equivalent, consistent with RV3/PPUBench findings)

e2e_image_level_results.interpretation: e2e outcome is bounded by g routing; h-side contributed 0 unparseable outputs

route_limitation_finding.statement: The frozen E2C-v3 g route (LoRA rank 8, 3000 steps, image->code) establishes same-person visual identities reliably (PPUBench held-out 1.000, SALMUBench 0.806) but does NOT generalize to attribute-class identities spanning many distinct faces: it memorizes training faces (train 0.943) instead of abstracting the defining cue (held-out 0.396, confusion spread across all signatures, including strong object cues like Bald 0.96/0.00).
route_limitation_finding.implication: For multi-face class identities the pipeline remains valid at the association level (C->Y), which is where the controlled granularity experiments (specific->subgroup->group, specific->numeric->range) live; image-level e2e claims must be scoped to same-person identity sources or gated g routing.
route_limitation_finding.collateral_wording: no observed collateral on the 2 tested retained identities; NOT a general zero-collateral claim
